target: Synthetic target: tile-server of Studio Cartografico Lunaria (fictitious)
method: A short list of threat categories (spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information_disclosure, denial_of_service, elevation_of_privilege) applied per entry point, sorted by blast radius. The category names follow the published STRIDE mnemonic [TO CONFIRM with legal]; no conformance to any standard is claimed.
context: Solo-founder context: one person holds every role, so each accepted risk names a role account, a date and a review date instead of relying on a team to remember it.

threats.statement: A key committed to the repository is read by anyone who can clone it.
threats.mitigation: No covered secret in the tree; if one leaks, the compromised-key playbook rotates and revokes it.

threats.statement: A compromised handler reaches the container runtime and takes the host.
threats.mitigation: No service mounts the runtime socket.

threats.statement: A request reaches the administration interface without an authenticated identity.
threats.mitigation: The admin router sits behind forward-auth.

threats.statement: A client forges the identity headers that the gate is supposed to set.
threats.mitigation: The forward-auth middleware does not trust forwarded headers from the client.

threats.statement: The administration port is published on a public interface.
threats.mitigation: The admin service publishes its port on the private bind only.

threats.statement: The public network reaches the database directly, bypassing the API.
threats.mitigation: Segmentation: the database is on the data network only and publishes no port; the API is not on the public network.

threats.statement: Debug output exposes internals through the public application.
threats.mitigation: DEBUG is off in the production environment file and no debug route is public.

threats.statement: An API call cannot be attributed afterwards because request logs are kept for a short time only.
threats.rationale: Low value of the data served by the public API; revisit when write endpoints are added.

threats.statement: A volumetric flood on the single gateway takes the public site down.
threats.rationale: One gateway, no upstream scrubbing: accepted for a public map viewer; rate limiting covers only the application layer.

threats.statement: A single client exhausts the application handlers.
threats.mitigation: Rate limiting on the public application router.
